A1.justification: Both complete, readable 20-page PDFs describe the same InPose work. Text, equations, tables, figures, proofs, implementation details, and supplementary results support comparison, including material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original AMASS pose-estimation experiments, body-shape and measurement-noise tests, ablations, and qualitative failure cases in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports additional body-shape comparisons, inverse-guidance experiments, runtime measurements, and head-conditioned failure-case outputs.

M1.justification: The proposed rotation-conditioned prior, location-based inverse guidance, differential parameterization, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. InPose (head) corresponds to v1's existing InPose +lhead variant. The newly evaluated local/global guidance alternatives are comparison methods, not changes to the principal algorithm.

E1.justification: The AMASS datasets and pose-estimation task remain unchanged. v2 Table 2 adds milder body-shape scenarios: upper body scaled by 0.85 or 1.17, and arms by 0.85 with torso by 1.17. Existing extreme-shape scenarios remain covered by the principal methods.

E2.justification: v2 Table 5 adds Local(ΠGDM), Local(Gradient Descent), and Global(Gradient Descent) comparisons against InPose (head). The principal AvatarJLM and BoDiffusion baselines remain, although the separate head-variant comparison in Table 2 includes only BoDiffusion baselines. Removing 'DPS' from v1 Table 3's caption, now Table 4, does not change that table's actual comparators.

E3.justification: The original splits, pose metrics, resampling, and training/inference budgets are retained. The revised local-guidance experiment conditions on head position while zeroing hand positions, unlike v1's local-DPS test without position conditioning. v2 also introduces a throughput evaluation measured in samples per second on an RTX Titan.

E4.justification: The head-input ablation is revised to use milder shape variations, and Figure 12 adds head-conditioned outputs for existing failure cases. Appendix C replaces the qualitative local-DPS discussion with a numerical local/global guidance comparison. The existing noise, bone-length, representation, and location-input analyses remain; the preliminary foot-contact failure observation is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The added tables retain point-estimate reporting; experimental Gaussian noise is not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The original non-head body-shape scores and quantitative plots are retained. New Tables 2, 5, and 6 report milder-shape results, guidance comparisons, and throughput, including approximately 229 samples/second for InPose. Five extreme-shape head-variant result sets are omitted. The matching head-variant entries print UPE as 2.48 cm in v1 Table 1 and 2.47 cm in v2 Table 5. Figure 12 adds head-conditioned outcomes.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 corrects the second vector's indices from 3:6 to 4:6 in its norm and orthogonality conditions. Appendix A also changes the approximated conditional variable from r_M^T to r_M^0. The covariance derivation otherwise remains unchanged, and the old 3:6 indexing persists within the proof body.

C1.justification: Both versions claim zero-shot generalization across body shapes through a scale-free rotational prior and body-dependent location guidance. The rewritten introduction and conclusion retain this contribution and acknowledge weaker performance for the default training shape.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses the flexibility cost of head conditioning and suggests an unsound Gaussian approximation as a possible explanation for weaker default-shape performance. It frames required bone-length calibration as a limitation and explains the upper/lower-body tradeoff in Table 5. Appendix B softens the identity-covariance performance claim, while v1's foot-contact discussion is removed.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly advertises code at the existing project website, which v1 described as providing results and animations. Appendix C documents conditioning and masking for the new guidance comparisons and identifies the runtime hardware. The principal model size, sequence handling, training duration, batch size, and diffusion-step settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Rozet et al. (2024) and Yang et al. (2024), removes Han et al. (2020) and Stathopoulos et al. (2024), and drops the 1,000-step contrast with Xie et al. (2024). The duplicate Zheng references are consolidated rather than representing a removed work. Overall positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the introductory background, rewrites the conclusion, moves and revises limitations from Appendix D into Section 6, and adds acknowledgements and conference headers. It also edits grammar and standardizes terminology such as '6D' and 'body shape'; the overarching organization remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The original body-shape tables are regrouped into v2 Tables 1 and 3, with results exchanged between the main text and appendix. Tables 2, 5, and 6 are added. Figure 12 gains a head-variant column and failure annotations, and Figure 10 moves to the final page. Other figure graphics are retained, with localized caption and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The guidance comparisons, runtime measurements, and expanded failure-case evaluation provide useful evidence about practical tradeoffs. Revised limitations and explicit code-access information improve transparency. These gains are limited by removal of earlier extreme-shape head-variant results and preliminary negative observations, while the Gaussian approximation remains unresolved. The core method and most supporting results are unchanged.
